newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle sell at $69, moderate - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle sell at $69, moderate - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Wednesday sold at $69.00 per cwt in moderate volume, steady with the bulk of Tuesday's sales, feedlot sources said.
About 15,500 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, bringing the weekly total near 85,000, they said.
In Kansas, an estimated 21,800 head sold, which brought week-to-date sales near 74,000, the sources said.
Attempts to sell cattle at $70.00 were rebuffed by sharply lower CME live cattle futures, sources said.

Cattle futures were said to be sharply lower on rumors that a Indiana rose farmer may have died from Creutzfeld-Jakob Disease, which British scientists last year said could be linked to bovine spongiform encephalopathy or "mad cow" disease.
This week's active fed cattle sales at $69.00 were $2.00 above the bulk of last week's trade.

Fed cattle prices could be pressured by the lower CME cattle futures, ideas that prices were near a top and by trade estimates that Friday's USDA Cattle-On-Feed report would show heavy numbers of cattle on feed, market sources said.

Analysts' estimates on the report put the number of cattle on feed in feedlots with 1,000 head or more capacity in the seven key states at 107.6 percent of a year ago as of April 1. March placements estimates averaged 103.3 percent of a year ago and March marketings estimates averaged 100.6 percent.
